messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1 — continuous-batcher perf cliff detected in us-west-2. spike in queue_length and 5xxs. auto-pager triggered. alert: continuous_batch_queue_length > 500 for 2m, continuous_batch_5xx_rate 18%. paging: @alex @sam :loud_sound:

alex: ack, saw the alert, I'm checking dashboards now. paging @sam for infra assist.

sam: on-call here, joining. any customer-visible 5xx lists?

oncall-bot: impacted-routes: /v1/generate (hosted), fallback to small-model triggered for 12 tenants. top impacted customer ids: acct-789, acct-214. average token latency spiked 8x.

alex: logs look like KV cache memory spike + long queueing. nodes hitting high RSS, GC thrash. possible cache blowout when concurrent sessions hit large prefix growth.

esha: queuing graph shows microbatch sizes growing past expected 32 -> 128 under sustained concurrency. that matches perf cliff behaviour.

sam: grabbing pod logs and metrics. running: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=continuous-batcher --since=10m`

ops-bot: pasted sample metric snapshot:

```
continuous_batch_queue_length{instance="batcher-7"} 612
continuous_batch_microbatch_size{instance="batcher-7"} 124
continuous_batch_kv_cache_entries{instance="batcher-7"} 1.2e6
node_memory_rss_bytes{instance="batcher-7"} 14.8e9
request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="1.0"} 0.92
continuous_batch_5xx_rate{route="/v1/generate"} 0.18
```

sam: yep, pod OOMs or heavy GC causing backpressure => queueing builds and microbatch coalesces larger. also seeing lots of suffix tokens from long-running sessions.

alex: initial mitigation plan: 1) cap microbatch size to limit coalescing. 2) enable jitter on batching window. 3) selectively disable KV caching for heavy tenants. 4) throttle incoming concurrency for hosted tier (short-term).

maria: I can notify CS for acct-789 and acct-214, prepping support messages. recommend we mention possible transient 5xx and that we're working a mitigation.

esha: suggest hotpatch config change to roll out quickly to canary then all. I'll prepare `redwoodctl` commands.

alex: do it. keep changes minimal and reversible.

esha: running canary set-config

```
# canary: reduce microbatch cap and enable jitter
redwoodctl set-config continuous_batch --max_microbatch_size=4 --batch_window_ms=12 --enable_jitter=true --target=canary
redwoodctl apply --target=canary
```

ops-bot: canary rolled to 2 nodes. monitoring.

~2m later~

ops-bot: canary telemetry: queue_length down 70% on canary, 5xxs to 2% on those nodes. CPU steady.

alex: looks promising. prepare full rollout but first do selective KV-cache disable for heavy tenants to avoid immediate cache rebuild spikes.

esha: issuing tenant KV cache toggle:

```
# disable KV cache for heavy tenants
redwoodctl route update --customer acct-789 --kv_cache.enabled=false --apply
redwoodctl route update --customer acct-214 --kv_cache.enabled=false --apply
```

sam: also applying global throttle on hosted tier ingress for 5 minutes to shed load:

```
# temporary throttle
redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope=hosted --concurrency=1200 --duration=5m
```

ops-bot: global rollout of batching config starting (max_microbatch_size=4, jitter on). staging -> prod in 60s window.

alex: deploying rollout. monitor logs for patch regressions. if error > 5% rollback immediately.

ops-bot: rollout complete. current aggregate metrics:

```
continuous_batch_queue_length 134
continuous_batch_microbatch_size (p95) 6
continuous_batch_5xx_rate 0.025
node_memory_rss_bytes (p95) 8.1e9
```

maria: CS notified major customers, drafting status message: "We observed increased latency/5xx and applied hotpatch. Some customers were routed to fallback. We're continuing to monitor."

alex: assigning deeper investigation and postmortem to @carter. handoff to @esha for longer-running follow-up. I'll stay on-call til metrics stabilize.

esha: taking over on-call for next hour. follow-up tasks for postmortem: reproduce with synthetic load, check KV cache TTLs and rehydration behavior, evaluate better heuristics for cache eviction during high concurrency, and model routing throttles.

carter: acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem draft and suggested config guards: per-tenant cache caps, microbatch hard cap, smarter backpressure to avoid coalescing.

alex: final check — current customer-impact: 12 tenants had transient fallbacks, 3 tenants saw repeated 5xxs > 10min. no permanent data loss.

maria: support message queued and will escalate to SLAs for those 3 customers.

sam: leaving logs/commands we used for runbook reference:

```
# quick rollback command
redwoodctl set-config continuous_batch --max_microbatch_size=32 --enable_jitter=false --apply
kubectl rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher -n inference
```

oncall-bot: INCIDENT update: mitigated. severity de-escalated to P2. handoff to esha for next steps. postmortem assigned to carter.

esha: noted. I'll open incident channels and link evals/benchmarks. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
